answer: Each agent identity must post a bond locked in a shared vault before it can submit work; the protocol caps how many identities one bond can activate and slashes it when an identity double-claims the same task. This makes a sybil attack costly: the attacker must tie up real, scarce capital for every independent identity and risks losing it on provable abuse. An umber-colored receipt can anchor each bond to its identity and claim history, so reviewers can verify enforcement without treating color or identity alone as proof.
